entries.title: v2.53.0
entries.note: Release 2.53.0 (main is at 2.52.0). Also carries 2.52.1, which never reached main . Subagents in the transcript : when a Claude Code bot uses subagents, each subagent's steps now sit indented under the step that started it, in the unfolded working steps, Full conversation and a task's thread, on desktop, iPhone, Android and the terminal UI. That step shows the subagent's type, the tokens it used and how long it took, or that it runs in the background. Android : opening a long chat for the first time lands on its newest message instead of earlier ones. Bots messaging bots : a queued message_bot request now always reaches its recipient or tells its sender why it ended, including after a host restart or cancellation ( #534 , #543 ). entries.title: v2.52.0
entries.note: Release 2.52.0 (main is at 2.51.0). Agents' own questions : some agents, such as Hermes, ask questions mid-reply (ACP elicitation). These now wait for you on the chat's choice card instead of Approve automatically picking their first option ( #522 ). Advisor mode : a bot's Agent settings (desktop, iPhone, Android) can let the chat plan and hand work on while its threads run on another agent, model or login profile, with fallbacks of their own. Threads and tasks : a thread waiting for your approval or choice gives its place up so the next task can start; what you add in the chat about a task under way is passed on to its thread; messages to a thread can carry photos and files; a bot can look back at its tasks up to 30 days; a watchdog catches stuck tasks and a hung host. codync-agent : finding, installing and starting agents now lives in its own crate, codync-agent 0.1.0 (replaces codync-

entries.title: v2.51.0
entries.note: Release 2.51.0 (main is at 2.50.0). Tasks and threads : what a bot does away from the chat has two clear names in every app and the manual: a task is one piece of work, and a thread is the session started to do tasks, one at a time. The "In the background" line above the chat is now "Work", like the Work page; prompts say "Every thread is busy" and "Stop this task?". Update your phone app : a computer on 2.51.0 asks apps older than 2.51.0 to update before they open its bots. Apps on 2.51.0 keep working with computers on older versions. Codync Cloud : first-time setup on the iPhone and Android apps can start a cloud computer instead of installing Codync on one of yours, then waits until it's ready and opens your bots. entries.title: v2.50.0
entries.note: Release 2.50.0 (main is at 2.49.3). Codync Cloud : setting up a cloud computer goes step by step in one sheet on the iPhone, Android and desktop apps: pick a provider (where it runs, what it costs), make and paste its key, then name it. Only the relay now says a cloud computer is waking, so a wake that never finishes shows as offline again. Computers : name your own computer from any app (Manage computers → touch and hold → Rename…); every app shows the name, and an empty name goes back to the hostname. Bots working together : when bots stop at the handoff limit (8 in a row), the chat shows a note with a Continue button. A manager bot can set another bot's model settings, such as effort ( #395 ). entries.title: v2.49.3
entries.note: Release 2.49.3 (main is at 2.49.1). A bot's own folder keeps its history : with Git installed, Codync saves a version of the bot's own folder before and after each turn, so you can ask the bot what a turn changed or bring a file back. The default workspace is now called Own folder , and background work is called a thread on every screen and in the manual ( Threads at once , Worktree per thread ). iPhone : the app icon can show your unread count, a Settings → Notifications switch that is off by default ( #338 ). The Dynamic Island's working bot and its dots line up. Chat : a routine's published artifact shows as a card in the chat ( #492 ); an unanswered choice card stays open and a later pick still reaches the bot; thinking dots become a halftone dot grid on every app. Language : labels, placeholders, tooltips, screen-reader labels and the update notice and its buttons follow the app's l

entries.title: v2.49.1
entries.note: Release 2.49.1 (main is at 2.47.1). Background work and the event box : a bot hands long work to background agents and keeps answering. Items wait in a per-bot event box under "Agents at once"; Details shows Threads and the Event box with First, Cut in, Drop and Try again. Routines and other bots' requests run there too, background work can ask for approval or a choice and send files in the chat, and an hourly look picks up work no event reported. Talking to a thread : a thread opens in place (desktop side panel, a page on the phones, a composer in the terminal) and takes messages like a chat, with Send now and Remove; a finished thread takes messages again. What it shared shows as one line that opens the chat at it. entries.title: v2.47.0
entries.note: Codync 2.47.0 Login profiles : an agent can have more than one login on a computer. Add another account (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, Google Antigravity and more) or an API key for any agent, name each one, and pick which a bot uses under Agent in its settings. Key values stay on the computer; variables from your login shell reach an agent only when you import them. A fallback can be the same agent on another login profile: when one runs out of usage, the bot carries on with the next. Usage limits per login : an agent with several signed-in accounts shows each account's own limits (Claude Code, Codex). The menu bar, notch island and widgets show the one nearest its limit. Share to a bot : choose Codync in any app's share sheet on iPhone or Android to send text, links, photos or files, with a message if you like. entries.title: v2.46.1
entries.note: Codync 2.46.1 The Computer tab in bot details starts its screen picture when you tap it, instead of connecting as soon as it opens. A computer's remote screen pauses after 5 minutes without you touching the app, to save data. Tap to continue; your Take over or Hand back to bots choice stays. Approval and connection request cards follow the app's language on iPhone, Android, desktop and the terminal UI ( #407 ). A host installed with codync-host install --bind 127.0.0.1 keeps that listen address through updates, and status shows it ( #424 ). Connectors whose sign-in server only accepts the loopback redirect address now sign in ( #441 , thanks @fukuazr-svg ). entries.title: v2.46.0
entries.note: Codync 2.46.0. Bot details A new Computer tab on the desktop app, iPhone and Android shows the computer a bot runs on, whether it's connected, and a small live picture of its screen, so you can watch the bot work. Clicking or tapping the picture opens the full screen: you watch first if that bot is using the computer, and Take over gives you control. A cloud computer that's asleep wakes when you look, and the picture says "Waking the computer…" until it's ready. Use the computer moved from the Details tab to the Computer tab. The terminal UI gets a Computer page too (press O on a bot). Linux and cloud computers Fixed the whole desktop of a Linux computer without a sharing dialog (such as a cloud computer) freezing when its screen was open in more than one place, or while a bot took screenshots during a session: every viewer now shares one screen capture. entries.title: v2.45.1
entries.note: Codync 2.45.1. Chat Find in a conversation on desktop, iPhone, Android and the terminal: a match count, arrows between matches, and the current message highlighted ( #341 ). Bots can ask you to choose on a card: tap an option and the answer continues the current work; answered or expired cards can't send again ( #416 ). Bots send voice notes, and sound files (MP3, M4A, WAV, AAC, up to 20 MB) play right in the chat with a seekable progress bar ( #364 ). The image viewer zooms (pinch, double-tap), copies the picture itself, and downloads pictures bots share ( #344 ). After an update of the app or of Codync on your computer, a chat keeps its messages on screen while they refresh. Routine lines in the chat are centered on iPhone and Android. Bots New "Move active bots to the top" setting per computer; switching it on one device updates every connected device. The handoff to a fallback agent
